To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 2/s spike-and-wave complexes of the Lennox-Gastault syndrome result from a thalamofrontal pathway, with the thalamic component preceding by about 35 msec that of the frontal component.

interictal spike wave complexes of the ILGS originate from the mesencephalothalamic reticular formation, and that their propagation from subcortical to cortical structures is mediated by the thalamocortical system.

(a) interictal SKW of the Lennox-Gastault syndrome result from ascending reticulo-cortical impulses impinging upon frontal cortical neurons; and (b) the centromedian nucleus of the thalamus is the main relay station of these impulses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of interictal spike wave complexes (SKW).
the temporal-spatial correlation between cortical and sub-cortical 2/s SKWs, which is the basis of the neuroaugmentive treatment of the ILGS.
the analysis of the interictial 2/s SKWs in the ILGS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ILGS is a disorder of the ascending reticulo-cortical system, in which the mesencephalo-thalamic and thalamo-cortical systems are involved.
the 2/s SKWs of the ILGS originate from the mesencephalo-thalamic region and propagate via the thalamocortical pathways.
the ILGS 2/s SKWs are generated in the thalamocortical network, which is composed by the mesencephalothalamic reticular system and the frontal cortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ILGS represents a specific form of a generalized epilepsy, which is caused by the abnormal activity of the mesencephalo-thalamo-cortical system.

the 2/s SKWs are generated in the thalamic reticular nuclei, from which they spread to the thalamic relay nuclei and to the frontal cortical regions, where the spike-wave complex attains maximal amplitude.
the 2/s SKWs of the ILGS represent a specific type of the 2/s spike and wave discharges (SWD).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Idiopathic Lennnox-Gastaut Syndrome (ILGS) results from a dysfunction of the mesencephalo-thalamic reticulocortical system.

in patients with atypical absence seizures, there is a strong correlation between the cortical spike and the negative spike in the thalamus, which suggests that the negative spike is the thalamic equivalent to the cortical spike.
the ictal and interictal EEG discharges of the ILGS may result from the same pathophysiological mechanism.
